tagline: Twenty-eight back roads that go wherever the creek goes.
intro: This is less one road than a net of 28 of them, about 27 miles in northern New Castle County between Route 52 and Route 48, laid along the contours of Red Clay Creek and its side streams. They run past pastoral flood plains and up steep wooded hillsides.

Yorklyn, once called Auburn Mills, kept a 19th-century trade in grist, snuff and paper along the creek. The Wilmington and Western, a line opened in 1872 and run for heritage trains since 1966, follows the valley from Greenbank toward Hockessin. Floods in 1999 and 2003 swept away its timber trestles. The new ones are steel.

moments.title: Ashland Covered Bridge
moments.text: This Town lattice truss of about 1860 beside the Ashland Nature Center has been battered by oversized trucks that ignored the signs, in 2011 and again in 2014.

moments.title: Auburn Valley State Park
moments.text: At Auburn Heights, above the old Marshall family mills in Yorklyn, volunteers keep 15 Stanley steam cars in running order while a miniature coal-powered train circles the estate.

moments.title: Wooddale Bridge
moments.text: The covered bridge of about 1850 was destroyed by flooding from Tropical Storm Henri in 2003 and rebuilt of Bongossi wood with the road raised five feet, in case the creek tries again.
